content.title: A Success Model at the End of Its Life Cycle: 30 Years of Regionalised Regional Rail in Germany
content.abstract: On 1 January 1996, Germany transferred responsibility for regional passenger rail services from the federal government to the states. Three decades later, passenger-kilometres have doubled and competitive tendering has lowered operating costs substantially, making regionalisation the most successful element of the German rail reform. Its organisational model, however, has reached the end of its life cycle: tenders now attract on average only 1.3 bids, 26 contracting authorities and some 60 transport associations maintain overlapping structures, rolling-stock procurement has repeatedly shifted
